title: Interplay of nonrelativistic and relativistic spin splittings in altermagnets
authors: Daegeun Jo, Peter M. Oppeneer, Mohsen Yarmohammadi
abstract: Despite their compensated magnetic moments, altermagnets (AMs) exhibit nonrelativistic spin splitting (NRSS) that offers routes to spintronic functionality without relying on relativistic spin-orbit coupling. However, how NRSS influences relativistic phenomena remains largely unexplored. Here we show that NRSS plays a crucial role in reshaping the Rashba effect in AMs with broken inversion symmetry. Using a tight-binding model, we demonstrate that Rashba spin splitting, whose magnitude is typically limited by the strength of spin-orbit coupling, is governed by NRSS energy scales. The resulting Rashba bands combined with NRSS generate anomalously large charge-to-spin conversion with a Néel-vector-tunable spin polarization. First-principles calculations for the noncentrosymmetric AM GdAlSi corroborate the emergence of these effects in a real system. Our results reveal the interplay between nonrelativistic and relativistic effects in AMs and identify them as fertile platforms for spin-orbitronic applications.
summary: This work explores how nonrelativistic spin splitting (NRSS) significantly modifies the relativistic Rashba effect in altermagnets (AMs). By combining theoretical modeling with DFT calculations on GdAlSi, the authors show that this interplay leads to an anomalously enhanced charge-to-spin conversion efficiency. This identifies AMs as promising platforms for advanced spintronic applications.
main_problem: The paper investigates the interplay between nonrelativistic spin splitting (NRSS) and relativistic spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in altermagnets (AMs), specifically how NRSS modifies the Rashba effect.
main_result: The interplay allows for anomalously large charge-to-spin conversion with a spin polarization that can be tuned by the Néel vector, demonstrating a distinctive enhancement in AMs compared to ferromagnetic systems.
method: The study employs a combination of theoretical tight-binding modeling and first-principles Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations.
model_or_system: The system studied is the altermagnet GdAlSi, modeled using DFT (FLAPW method) and supplemented by a generic 2D d-wave tight-binding model Hamiltonian incorporating NRSS, SOC, and Inversion Symmetry Breaking (ISB).
key_observables: Rashba spin splitting, charge-to-spin conversion efficiency (Spin Edelstein Effect, SEE), and sublattice-resolved spin polarizations.
important_parameters: The relative energy scales of SOC ($E_{SOC}$), NRSS ($E_{NRSS}$), and ISB ($E_{ISB}$), particularly the moderate regime where $E_{SOC} \ll E_{NRSS} \lesssim E_{ISB}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the tight-binding model approximation and the inclusion of a Hubbard U term for Gd 4f electrons in the DFT calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate band structures showing the evolution of Rashba splitting under varying NRSS strengths, and show spin textures and orbital angular momentum polarization on the Fermi surface for both AM and FM models.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework using a tight-binding model to analyze the interplay of NRSS and SOC. It then uses DFT on GdAlSi to corroborate these effects, calculating the SEE and demonstrating the enhancement due to the AM nature.
why_interesting: While the primary focus is on spintronics, the detailed analysis of spin-momentum locking and spin-orbit coupling mechanisms in magnetic materials is highly relevant to understanding topological and spin-related phenomena in condensed matter physics.
